text: Symptoms: Warning divergent transitions; unreliable estimates Diagnosis: Solutions: 1. Increase adapt_delta 0.95 0.99 2. Reparameterize (bhfvar already uses non-centered) 3. Check data issues (extreme weights, sparse domains)
code: # Check which iterations diverged library(rstan) sampler_params <- get_sampler_params(fit$stanfit, inc_warmup = FALSE) divergent <- sapply(sampler_params, function(x) sum(x[, "divergent__"])) print(divergent)

title: Model Diagnostics and Convergence Checking
text: Symptoms: R-hat > 1.05; chains don’t overlap trace plots Diagnosis: Solutions: 1. Run longer (increase iter) 2. Increase warmup period 3. Check multimodality identification issues
code: # Check which parameters have high R-hat summ <- summary(fit$stanfit)$summary high_rhat <- summ[summ[, "Rhat"] > 1.05, , drop = FALSE] print(rownames(high_rhat))

title: Model Diagnostics and Convergence Checking

code: # Check which parameters have low ESS summ <- summary(fit$stanfit)$summary low_ess <- summ[summ[, "n_eff"] < 400, , drop = FALSE] print(rownames(low_ess))

text: Consider population NN units partitioned SS non-overlapping domains (e.g., states). binary outcome YY, population proportion domain ss : ps=∑∈UsYiNs p_s = \frac{\sum_{\U_s} Y_i}{N_s}  UsU_s set population units domain ss Ns=|Us|N_s = |U_s|. population-level variance decomposition partitions total variance -domain within-domain components: Var(Y)=∑s=1Sπs(ps−p‾)2⏟-domain+∑s=1Sπs⋅ps(1−ps)⏟Within-domain \text{Var}(Y) = \underbrace{\sum_{s=1}^S \pi_s (p_s - \bar{p})^2}_{\text{-domain}} +  \underbrace{\sum_{s=1}^S \pi_s \cdot p_s(1-p_s)}_{\text{Within-domain}}  πs=Ns/N\pi_s = N_s/N population shares p‾=∑sπsps\bar{p} = \sum_s \pi_s p_s. text: Even without informative sampling, estimating domain proportions p̂s\hat{p}_s small samples introduces noise: p̂s=ps+es,E[es]=0,Var(es)=Vs \hat{p}_s = p_s + e_s, \quad E[e_s] = 0, \quad \text{Var}(e_s) = V_s naive -domain variance estimator biased upward: E[σ̂between2]≈σbetween2+∑s=1SπsVs E[\hat{\sigma}^2_{\text{}}] \approx \sigma^2_{\text{}} +  \sum_{s=1}^S \pi_s V_s second term represents average sampling variance—noise masquerades signal.

title: Methodology: The Bayesian Hybrid Framework
text: Standard likelihood-based inference treats observations exchangeable: L(θ)=∏∈𝒮P(Yi∣θ) L(\theta) = \prod_{\\mathcal{S}} P(Y_i \mid \theta) informative sampling, yields biased population estimates -sampled subgroups receive equal weight despite representing smaller population shares.

title: Methodology: The Bayesian Hybrid Framework
text: Bayesian Pseudo-Likelihood approach (Savitsky & Toth, 2016) exponentiates likelihood contribution survey weight: LBPL(Y∣θ)=∏∈𝒮[P(Yi∣θ)]wi* L_{\text{BPL}}(Y \mid \theta) = \prod_{\\mathcal{S}} [P(Y_i \mid \theta)]^{w_i^*} resulting pseudo-posterior : PBPL(θ∣Y,w)∝LBPL(Y∣θ)⋅P(θ) P_{\text{BPL}}(\theta \mid Y, w) \propto L_{\text{BPL}}(Y \mid \theta) \cdot P(\theta) approach: Upweights observations representing large population subgroups Downweights -sampled subgroups Achieves design-consistent inference population parameters

title: Methodology: The Bayesian Hybrid Framework
text: multilevel models, scale weights matters (Rabe-Hesketh & Skrondal, 2006). Raw weights summing population size cause: Inflated “apparent” cluster sizes Biased variance component estimates bhfvar package uses Method 2 scaling (Pfeffermann et al., 1998): wi*=wi⋅n∑∈𝒮wi w_i^* = w_i \cdot \frac{n}{\sum_{\\mathcal{S}} w_i} scales weights sum sample size nn, preserving relative importance stabilizing estimation.

title: Methodology: The Bayesian Hybrid Framework
text: Hybrid GLMM models log-odds outcome: ηi=α+ustate[]+upsu[] \eta_i = \alpha + u_{\text{state}[]} + u_{\text{psu}[]} random effects: ustate[s]∼N(0,σstate2) u_{\text{state}[s]} \sim N(0, \sigma^2_{\text{state}}) upsu[j]∼N(0,σpsu2) u_{\text{psu}[j]} \sim N(0, \sigma^2_{\text{psu}}) outcome follows: Yi∣ηi∼Bernoulli(logit−1(ηi)) Y_i \mid \eta_i \sim \text{Bernoulli}(\text{logit}^{-1}(\eta_i))

title: Methodology: The Bayesian Hybrid Framework
text: model “hybrid” two senses: Inference approach: Combines design-based weights (representativeness) model-based structure (variance components) Random effects structure: Includes substantive effects (states, research target) nuisance effects (PSUs, design artifacts) structure correctly partitions variance: σstate2\sigma^2_{\text{state}} captures substantive domain heterogeneity net design-induced clustering.

title: Methodology: The Bayesian Hybrid Framework
text: identifiability interpretability, apply centering: State effects use population-weighted centering: ∑s=1Sπs⋅ustate[s]=0 \sum_{s=1}^S \pi_s \cdot u_{\text{state}[s]} = 0 ensures α\alpha represents population mean log-odds. PSU effects use within-stratum centering: ∑j∈hupsu[j]=0∀h \sum_{j \h} u_{\text{psu}[j]} = 0 \quad \forall h prevents confounding stratum PSU effects.

title: Methodology: The Bayesian Hybrid Framework
text: bhfvar package uses weakly informative priors: non-centered parameterization improves MCMC sampling: ustate[s]=σstate⋅zstate[s],zstate[s]∼N(0,1) u_{\text{state}[s]} = \sigma_{\text{state}} \cdot z_{\text{state}[s]}, \quad  z_{\text{state}[s]} \sim N(0, 1)

title: Methodology: The Bayesian Hybrid Framework
text: latent logit scale, variance components decompose additively: Var(η)=σstate2+σpsu2+π23 \text{Var}(\eta) = \sigma^2_{\text{state}} + \sigma^2_{\text{psu}} + \frac{\pi^2}{3} level-1 variance π2/3\pi^2/3 comes logistic distribution. ICC logit scale : ICCA=σstate2σstate2+σpsu2+π2/3 \text{ICC}_A = \frac{\sigma^2_{\text{state}}}{\sigma^2_{\text{state}} + \sigma^2_{\text{psu}} + \pi^2/3}

title: Methodology: The Bayesian Hybrid Framework
text: compute variance probability scale, transform state effects using Zeger marginal adjustment (Zeger et al., 1988): ps=logit−1(c⋅(α+ustate[s])) p_s = \text{logit}^{-1}(c \cdot (\alpha + u_{\text{state}[s]}))  : c=11+0.346⋅σstate2 c = \sqrt{\frac{1}{1 + 0.346 \cdot \sigma^2_{\text{state}}}} -state variance probability scale: Varbetween=∑s=1Sπs(ps−p‾)2 \text{Var}_{\text{}} = \sum_{s=1}^S \pi_s (p_s - \bar{p})^2 Within-state (Bernoulli) variance: Varwithin=∑s=1Sπs⋅ps(1−ps) \text{Var}_{\text{within}} = \sum_{s=1}^S \pi_s \cdot p_s(1-p_s)

title: Methodology: The Bayesian Hybrid Framework
text: de-attenuated estimand corrects finite-sample variance inflation: Varbetween*=max⁡(0,Varbetween−∑s=1SπsV̂s) \text{Var}_{\text{}}^{*} = \max\left(0, \text{Var}_{\text{}} -  \sum_{s=1}^S \pi_s \hat{V}_s\right) V̂s\hat{V}_s design-based sampling variance state ss, estimated via Taylor linearization. correction applied within posterior: MCMC iteration, subtract estimated sampling variance compute de-attenuated ICC, properly propagating uncertainty.

title: Extract Variance Decomposition Results — variance_decomposition
text: function extracts three sets variance components: Estimand (Policy, logit scale) Variance decomposition latent logit scale. icc_state = sigma_state^2 / (sigma_state^2 + sigma_psu^2 + pi^2/3) Estimand B (Descriptive, probability scale) Variance decomposition observed probability scale. icc_prob = Var(p_s) / (Var(p_s) + E(p_s(1-p_s))) Estimand * (Policy adjusted, de-attenuated) Estimand B finite-sample variance inflation removed. icc_deatten = (Var(p_s) - V_hat) / (Var(p_s) - V_hat + E(p_s(1-p_s)))
